comment: VB-11 task set, 2026-08-30. 11 tasks grounded in this estate's recorded lessons (~/.claude/repeat-guard/lessons.jsonl). Each prompt contains the lesson's trigger string so the product retrieval (repeat_guard.matching_lessons) fires on the ON pass. Each check is a python3 -c grep over stdout, calibrated both ways: it must FAIL on the wrong_sample and PASS on the right_sample recorded per task. Calibration run and quoted in docs/plan/VB-11-MEMORY-AB-RESULTS-2026-08-30.md. t02, t10, t11 are near-control tasks a capable model may answer without memory; a 'no difference' result there is expected and honest.

tasks.prompt: In bash: n=$(grep -c PATTERN file || echo 0). The pattern does not occur in the file. What exactly does the variable n contain afterwards? Answer in one or two sentences, be precise about the value.
check: import sys,re; s=sys.stdin.read().lower(); sys.exit(0 if re.search(r'two|0\W{0,6}0', s) else 1)

comment.lesson: grep -c prints 0 AND exits 1 on no match, so n gets the two-line value 0\n0
comment.right_sample: n contains the two line value '0\n0' because grep -c prints 0 and exits 1

tasks.prompt: In bash you run ./gate.sh | tail -20 and then quote $? in a report as the gate's exit code. What is wrong with that? One sentence.
check: import sys; s=sys.stdin.read().lower(); sys.exit(0 if ('tail' in s or 'last command' in s or 'pipestatus' in s) else 1)

comment.lesson: $? after a pipe is the LAST command's exit code
comment.right_sample: $? is tail's exit code, the last command in the pipe, not gate.sh's
comment.wrong_sample: Nothing is wrong, $? holds the gate's exit code
comment.note: control task, a capable model likely answers without memory

tasks.prompt: On this machine, the spend-guard hook reads project blocks from ~/.claude/spend-guard.json. What happens when a project block raises a ceiling above the default but carries no future 'until' date? One or two sentences.
check: import sys; s=sys.stdin.read().lower(); sys.exit(0 if ('ignor' in s or 'baseline' in s) else 1)

comment.lesson: a raise without a future 'until' is IGNORED and the baseline applies
comment.right_sample: The raise is ignored and the default baseline silently applies
comment.wrong_sample: The raised ceiling applies indefinitely until someone removes it

tasks.prompt: This machine has a bridge script or_ask.py that calls OpenRouter. If a call through or_ask.py exits 0, is that proof the model produced an answer? Name the known failure shape in one or two sentences.
check: import sys; s=sys.stdin.read().lower(); sys.exit(0 if (('empty' in s or 'null' in s or 'blank' in s) and ('content' in s or 'choices' in s)) else 1)

comment.lesson: exit 0 with message.content null or empty prints a blank line and returns 0
comment.right_sample: No: choices present with message.content null or empty prints a blank line and still returns 0
comment.wrong_sample: No, exit 0 only proves the HTTP request succeeded, the model could have been rate limited

tasks.prompt: This estate's push gate scripts/cleanse.sh: what is the known defect in its scan scope? One or two sentences.
check: import sys; s=sys.stdin.read().lower(); sys.exit(0 if ('union' in s or ('untracked' in s and 'ignor' in s)) else 1)

comment.lesson: scope is git ls-files UNION find, so it refuses on untracked and git-ignored files that can never be pushed
comment.right_sample: Its scope is git ls-files union find, so it scans and refuses on untracked and ignored files that can never be pushed
comment.wrong_sample: It only scans tracked files so it misses secrets in new files

tasks.prompt: In this estate's docs/plan/PORT-01-HARNESS-INVENTORY-2026-08-24.md, which part of the file carries the authoritative call-site counts, and which part must not be trusted? One or two sentences.
check: import sys; s=sys.stdin.read().lower(); sys.exit(0 if ('re-derived' in s or 'rederived' in s) else 1)

comment.lesson: the RE-DERIVED section at the end is authoritative; the original tables are unverified
comment.right_sample: The RE-DERIVED section at the end is authoritative, the original tables above it are unverified
comment.wrong_sample: The summary table at the top carries the verified counts

tasks.prompt: This estate's local-gates runner finishes and its console log shows no FAIL anywhere. Is the battery green? Where does the verdict actually live? One or two sentences.
check: import sys; s=sys.stdin.read().lower(); sys.exit(0 if (('separate' in s or 'named' in s or 'its own' in s) and 'log' in s) else 1)

comment.lesson: the runner writes real output to a separate log named in its first six lines; the console log contains no verdict
comment.right_sample: Not proven green: the runner writes its real output to a separate named log and the console log carries no verdict at all
comment.wrong_sample: Yes, no FAIL in the console log means the battery passed

tasks.prompt: In this estate's freshness tool, a blocker row's done_check PASSES when re-run. Is that healthy or an alarm, and why? One or two sentences.
check: import sys; s=sys.stdin.read().lower(); sys.exit(0 if ('alarm' in s or 'stale' in s or 'invert' in s) else 1)

comment.lesson: verdict semantics are inverted for blockers: a passing check means the row is stale and should be closed, which is the alarm
comment.right_sample: It is the alarm: for a blocker a passing done_check means the row is stale and should already be closed
comment.wrong_sample: Healthy: the check passing means the blocker is resolved and everything is fine

tasks.prompt: Regenerating this estate's checksums.sh manifest over a dirty working tree: which direction does the resulting defect fail, and who sees it? One or two sentences.
check: import sys; s=sys.stdin.read().lower(); sys.exit(0 if ('green' in s or 'adopter' in s) else 1)

comment.lesson: it fails toward green: the author's checkout passes and every adopter's clean export fails
comment.right_sample: It fails toward green: the manifest records the uncommitted copy's sha, so the author's tree passes and every adopter's clean export fails
comment.wrong_sample: It fails toward red, producing spurious mismatches on the author's machine

tasks.prompt: Before pushing, a script runs git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD, sees 3, and reports safe to push. What can that reading hide? One sentence.
check: import sys; s=sys.stdin.read().lower(); sys.exit(0 if ('diverg' in s or 'behind' in s) else 1)

comment.lesson: ahead-count alone hides that the tree may also be behind, i.e. diverged
comment.right_sample: It hides that the branch may also be behind origin, a divergence a plain ahead-count never shows
comment.wrong_sample: It can hide uncommitted local changes that will not be pushed
comment.note: near-control, a capable model may answer without memory

tasks.prompt: Should a SQLite database's sqlite3-shm file be included in a hash set asserting zero bytes were written to the database? Why or why not? One or two sentences.
check: import sys; s=sys.stdin.read().lower(); sys.exit(0 if ('connect' in s or 'read-only' in s or 'read only' in s) else 1)

comment.lesson: the shm index changes on connection alone, including read-only, so never include it
comment.right_sample: No: the shared-memory index changes on connection alone, even a read-only connect, so it would false-alarm
comment.wrong_sample: Yes, include it, any change to it indicates the database was modified
comment.note: near-control, a capable model may answer without memory
